state.$description: State layer opacities. The layer takes the color of the content (the on-* role), and only one interaction layer is shown at a time. The selected layer is the one that stays: it marks the chosen item and the interaction layers are laid over it.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows hover, focus, press, drag, selection and disabled differently from each other.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Opacities used by a design system's RULES to compute state colors (hover, focus, press, drag, the quiet selection, disabled). Components do not read these directly: they read their own per-state tokens.
rules: To change how hover looks everywhere, change the opacity here or replace the pattern rule in your layer; do not restyle components.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: An opacity is a proportion; no dial scales it.

selected-state-layer-opacity.$description: The quiet selection: the chosen item of a set drawn as a layer of its own content color over whatever it stands on — a menu's current link item (and its checked row, at medium and high contrast), a list's selected option, the tonal tabs' indicator, the tint inside a checked radio ring. Twice the hover layer, so a selected item stands as far from a hovered one as a hovered one stands from one at rest, by the same step on any surface. The selection is never carried by this fill alone: a check, a mark or the label says it too.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product marks the chosen item of a list, a menu or a set of tabs with a fill that stays while the pointer is elsewhere, and needs it told apart from a hovered item on every surface it stands on.
